assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly distinctive voice that fuses classical scholarship, lyric, verse-novel, essay and visual book design. Autobiography of Red recasts Stesichorus as a modern queer coming-of-age story, and Nox is a book-object elegy built around a translation of Catullus 101. Formal invention is sustained rather than a single gesture, and the intellectual depth is high. The achievement lies in how translation, grief and desire become literary form.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would plausibly cover renewing the boundaries of poetry and the essay through an encounter with antiquity, in work that also includes Greek translations and drama. The scope is clear and does not overlap with other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Several decades of publication with consistent formal ambition and a stable reputation among readers of poetry. The oeuvre is deep and still developing, so timing is not a problem.
uncertainties: Much of the work depends on typography, page layout and the relation to ancient Greek texts. I cannot independently verify how fully these survive in translation.
It is uncertain whether the hybrid, scholarly mode would be read as the poetry or literature of broad ideal significance that Nobel's will describes.
Assessment relies on public knowledge of the major works. I have not re-read them and have not verified any source.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visionary, densely patterned prose in which body, memory, dream and metaphysics form an expansive imaginative cosmos. The Orbitor trilogy (Blinding in English) and Solenoid show ambitious architecture and a strongly individual voice. Imaginative scale and linguistic richness are the main strengths, with a tradition that includes Romanian poetry and the European fantastic.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would plausibly concern a visionary prose cosmos that builds on a poetic beginning. The poetry and the novels both belong to the case.
assessment.maturity: A long career from poetry in the 1980s to large late novels. The major works are sustained and coherent, and the development of the whole is visible.
uncertainties: Translation of long, stylistically dense Romanian prose into English and other languages may not carry its full sonority or syntax, and my judgment partly rests on reception.
The great length and the recurring motifs may raise a question about whether a few books or the whole oeuvre carry the weight.
No independent verification of the texts has been made.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fiction and memorial prose that recover the Tutsi world before and during the Rwandan genocide. The Barefoot Woman honors her mother in an austere form, and Our Lady of the Nile presents a girls' boarding school as a society under ideological pressure. The register is restrained yet precise, and the literary quality does not depend on the importance of the subject alone. The achievement lies in making testimony into durable literary form.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would cover literary witness and the recovery of a destroyed social world, written in French as a second language of exile. The scope is clear.
assessment.maturity: Her publishing career began relatively late, with a body of work that is shorter than that of many other candidates. The works are consistent in voice and theme, and the question is the breadth of the oeuvre.
uncertainties: The oeuvre is more compact and more thematically concentrated than others, which bears on the criterion of depth across a body of work.
The weight given to testimony versus invention in the narratives is a matter of interpretation, and my view rests on public knowledge and translations.
No independent verification of the texts has been made.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Meditative, morally attentive prose with a strongly recognizable voice. Housekeeping and the Gilead novels (Gilead, Home, Lila, Jack) bring theology, family, American history and ordinary perception into an unhurried, luminous style. The essays extend the same intellectual commitments. Formal range is narrower than in the more experimental candidates, but the depth of vision and the quality of the sentence are high.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would plausibly cover a contemplative, theologically informed realism in fiction and essay. The scope is clear, though the fiction is relatively small in volume.
assessment.maturity: From 1980 to the present with long intervals, and a late flowering in the Gilead cycle. The standing of the main works is established, and the cycle forms a coherent whole.
uncertainties: A small number of novels carries the case, and the volume of fiction is limited compared with others on the list.
Whether the heavily Protestant, American frame is felt as sufficiently wide in range is a matter for debate.
No independent verification of the texts has been made.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dense, compressed, intensely stylized French prose. Small Lives (Vies minuscules) turns obscure provincial lives into a meditation on origin, writing and vocation, and The Eleven builds a fictional account around a Revolution-era painting. Linguistic achievement is a central strength, with an influence from classical French prose. The oeuvre is small but exceptionally worked.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would plausibly concern a prose of extreme condensation that treats lives and art history as literary inquiry. The scope is narrow but precise.
assessment.maturity: Published since the mid-1980s, with a deliberately limited body of work of consistent quality. Established recognition in France.
uncertainties: The strongest qualities are tied to the texture of the French sentence, and I cannot judge how much is lost in English or Swedish translation.
The small size of the oeuvre could count against breadth, while the concentration counts for it.
No independent verification of the texts has been made.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Linguistic invention that brings Mozambican oral storytelling, neologism and magical elements into Portuguese-language novels about war, memory and the postcolonial condition. Sleepwalking Land (Terra sonâmbula) and Confession of the Lioness are well-known examples. The strength is a voice that renews the language from within. Poetry and short stories add to the body of work.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would plausibly concern renewal of Portuguese through Mozambican oral and cultural resources, in fiction and poetry. The scope is clear.
assessment.maturity: A career of several decades with a large body of work and international recognition. The pace of invention across late novels is less certain from my knowledge.
uncertainties: Much of the achievement is linguistic and neologistic, which is hard to assess in translation.
Some later work may rely on repeated strategies, and my knowledge of the full corpus is incomplete.
No independent verification of the texts has been made.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Writing in both Japanese and German that treats linguistic estrangement as a generative principle. The Emissary (a dystopian short novel) and Memoirs of a Polar Bear are examples of playful, precise invention that combines the fable, wordplay and social observation. The oeuvre spans fiction, poetry, essays and drama. Originality of method is strong.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would plausibly concern literature between languages and the creative use of translation and displacement. The bilingual corpus complicates coverage.
assessment.maturity: A career of several decades with a substantial body in two languages. Recognition is growing, and the sustained quality is clear in the works I know.
uncertainties: The German and Japanese bodies of work differ, and I have partial coverage of each, with only a part available in translation.
It is uncertain whether the lightness and wit of some work reaches the depth and breadth of the leading candidates.
No independent verification of the texts has been made.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large poetic sequences such as Purgatory and Anteparadise convert experience of dictatorship and loss into collective memorial form, with landscape-scale interventions like the sky-writing and the desert inscription. The poetry has a strongly individual voice and a significant ethical and visionary ambition. Formal radicalism and the link between poem and public act are the distinctive contributions.
assessment.attribution: A single writer. A citation would plausibly concern poetry as memorial and as a response to political violence. The scope is clear and mostly confined to poetry.
assessment.maturity: A career from the late 1970s to the present, with a coherent project and sustained standing in Latin American poetry. Later work extends the early themes.
uncertainties: Poetry that depends on Spanish rhythm and on specific historical context is difficult to evaluate through translation.
Some of the impact lies in the public or visual gestures and may not be fully captured as literary text.
No independent verification of the texts has been made.
